headline: Chinese AI developer Z.ai, also known as Zhipu AI, has unveiled GLM-Legal, a law-focused AI model that it says scores 19.2 percent on the strict Harvey LAB test of real law-firm work.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered 1: announced on 12 Oct (before the window) and the pool headline's comparison with Claude Fable 5 and Kimi K3 could not be confirmed.
importance_line: Law firms and in-house legal teams may get a specialised legal AI, but fewer than one task in five passes under that strict grading, the other test results come without figures, and MarkTechPost's headline claim of beating Claude Fable 5 and Kimi K3 is not in the account we could read.
summary: Unite.AI reports that Z.ai, the Chinese AI developer also called Zhipu AI, announced GLM-Legal on 12 Oct 2026, a legal-work model built on its lightweight GLM-5.3-Flash base, and says it reached a 19.2 percent all-pass rate on Harvey LAB, a test of real law-firm workflows across 24 practice areas, 12.5 percentage points above the base model. Z.ai also claims to match leading AI systems on two other legal tests without giving figures and is taking beta applications from law firms, legal-tech companies and legal teams; all results are the company's own.
notes: Original pool source MarkTechPost was blocked (403); Unite.AI credited instead. Announcement dated 12 Oct 2026, so stale against the 13 Oct window start. The 'beats Claude Fable 5 and Kimi K3' claim is MarkTechPost's and is not repeated as fact.
